profiles.meeting_scenario: One week before the SmartMLOps Studio paper artifact freeze and an internal lab demo, the evaluation lead and the platform integration lead meet to coordinate handoffs between the LLM-assisted IDE frontend and the automated MLOps backend. The context is that reported results span code generation support, automated pipeline configuration, reproducibility claims, and monitoring/retraining behavior on the UCI Adult and M5 datasets. The agenda is to align on which build will be used for the demo and artifact, what goes into the reproducibility package, how the 'traditional workflow' baseline reruns will be packaged, and what level of result validation is sufficient before freeze. The expected outcome is a concrete division of work and a shared-seeming plan for Thursday's handoff, even though several second-order assumptions remain unspoken.

members.name: Dr. Priya Raman
members.expertise: ML evaluation design, experiment reproducibility, benchmark reporting for applied LLM and MLOps systems
members.background: Priya is a senior PhD-level researcher who led the SmartMLOps Studio study design and wrote most of the evaluation section comparing the prototype against traditional ML workflows on Adult and M5.
members.private_state: She wants the artifact and demo to stay tightly aligned with the paper's reported numbers and screenshots, and is trying to avoid any last-minute changes that could create inconsistencies or force reruns she no longer has time to validate.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'traditional workflow baseline,' they still mean using the lab's pre-existing pipeline templates as long as the IDE is not auto-generating the configuration.
The 'current build' refers to the frozen evaluation branch used to produce the paper figures and screenshots, not whatever has changed on main since then.
The 'repro package' should include exactly what a reviewer needs to rerun the reported experiments and regenerate tables, not the full long-horizon monitoring and retraining loop.

If the team says the 'numbers line up,' that means the headline deltas are directionally consistent and within a small tolerance on a representative run rather than exact regeneration of every table row across all seeds.

members.name: Mateo Silva
members.role: Senior ML Platform Engineer and Integration Lead
members.expertise: MLOps orchestration, CI/CD for ML systems, experiment tracking, monitoring pipelines, and developer tooling integration
members.background: Mateo built the backend automation in SmartMLOps Studio, including data validation hooks, drift detection services, retraining triggers, and the IDE-to-pipeline handoff into the orchestration stack.
members.private_state: He wants the system to be represented as a true end-to-end platform rather than a polished research prototype, and is pushing for the artifact and demo to reflect the most recent integration fixes so the platform looks production-capable.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'traditional workflow baseline,' they mean a genuinely manual setup without relying on the team's old pipeline templates, because templates already embed operational expertise.
The 'current build' means the latest container and service state on main or in the staging registry, since that is what users would actually run and what his team maintains.
The 'repro package' should cover the full lifecycle claims in the paper, including monitoring, drift alerts, and retraining replay where those claims are discussed.

If the team says the 'numbers line up,' that means the official tables can be regenerated exactly, or near-exactly, using the agreed seeds and configs rather than just reproducing the same directional story.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the traditional workflow baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to rerunning the 'traditional workflow baseline' for the artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a non-LLM, non-integrated workflow that can still use the lab's existing Kubeflow/YAML starter templates, since the comparison is about lack of in-IDE automation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a fully manual workflow without those starter templates, because template reuse already removes much of the configuration burden SmartMLOps Studio is supposed to reduce.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as discussing the same published baseline and the phrase sounds established, so neither thinks to unpack exactly how much prior automation is still allowed inside 'traditional workflow.'

misalignment_points.topic: Which build is the current SmartMLOps Studio build
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the 'current build' or 'latest build' for the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the frozen evaluation branch and container image used for the paper's figures, logs, and screenshots.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the latest staging image from main, which includes a quiet patch to the retraining trigger and some assistant-side config handling.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many teams 'current build' is treated as an obvious reference, and both believe there is a single canonical version in circulation, even though research freeze and engineering latest are different objects.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They talk about what will go into the 'repro package' or 'artifact bundle.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the bundle covers rerunning the reported benchmark experiments and regenerating the tables for Adult and M5, with monitoring discussed only through precomputed logs or screenshots.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the bundle also includes the monitoring stack, drift replay, and retraining trigger path because those are part of the paper's lifecycle claims and should be executable, not merely illustrated.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'artifact bundle' sounds like a single shared deliverable, and both think they are being practical about what reviewers need, but they silently draw the boundary in different places.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the numbers to line up before freeze
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that before freeze they just need to make sure 'the numbers line up.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes one representative rerun per dataset that reproduces the same conclusion and stays close to the reported gains is enough to mark the results as validated for handoff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the final pipeline should regenerate the paper tables across the official seeds/configs with minimal deviation, since otherwise the artifact is not truly reproducible.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both care about reproducibility and use the same reassuring phrase, but each treats a different threshold as the obvious standard, so the conversation feels aligned rather than contentious.
